title: GNU Economy Ministry Bans Informal Commercial Imports Outside Banking Channels
detail: Tripoli-based Minister of Economy and Trade Suhail Abu Shiha issued Decision 449/2026 on Sunday, September 6, 2026, banning the import of goods and merchandise intended for trade outside official banking channels, effective September 30. The decision requires all banking, commercial, and customs requirements — including documentation proving a shipment's actual value — to be met before customs clearance, with an exemption for small traders importing within a specified annual limit under a valid business license and transitional provisions for shipments already in process. The ministry framed the move as an effort to control hard-currency use and curb foreign-currency and letters-of-credit fraud, against a backdrop of the dinar's continued slide on the parallel market and Central Bank Governor Naji Issa's still-pending August resignation.

media.caption: Libya bans informal commercial imports outside banking channels starting Sep 30, 2026

confidenceReason: Named ministry decision (449/2026) with specific provisions reported by Libya Herald; not yet independently corroborated by a second outlet despite multiple searches.

title: GNU Announces Arrest of Five-Member Cell Behind Zawiya and Tripoli Drone Sabotage Campaign
detail: Libya's Government of National Unity said on Sunday, September 6, 2026 that its Defense Ministry had dismantled a five-member 'sabotage cell' — including foreign nationals whose identities and nationalities it did not disclose — accused of carrying out the remotely detonated, explosive-laden drone strikes that hit oil storage tanks in Tripoli and Zawiya, the Zawiya power station, and other power and water facilities since early August. The government said the cell had also been preparing further attacks on the South Tripoli power station and other vital infrastructure, as well as against unnamed political, security, and military figures, describing the plot as 'broad and interconnected' and backed by unspecified 'external entities.' A ministry statement said 'dismantling this cell is not the end of the operation but the beginning of uncovering all the threads and extensions of this plot,' vowing to pursue anyone involved 'with an iron fist regardless of position or rank.' Authorities did not identify the suspects, disclose the foreign nationals' countries, or name which states or groups they believe supported the cell, leaving the drone campaign's ultimate sponsor unconfirmed even as the alleged operators are now in custody.

media.caption: GNU defense ministry announces the dismantling of a cell accused of drone attacks on Zawiya and Tripoli energy infrastructure, Sep 2026

confidenceReason: The GNU defense ministry's arrest announcement is corroborated by four independent Tier-2 wire/outlet reports (Africanews/AFP, Anadolu Agency, Arab News, The New Arab); the underlying claim that these five suspects are actually responsible for the unclaimed Aug 8-12 Zawiya campaign is the government's own unverified assertion, and no external sponsor or suspect identity has been confirmed.
